html:
An ancient city in northwest Anatolia, on a lake east of the Sea of Marmara, now the small Turkish town of İznik. It is best known for the church councils held there.

It was founded as a Greek city in the 300s BCE and became a leading city of Bithynia under the Romans. In 325 Constantine the Great called the bishops of the empire to the First Council of Nicaea, which issued the Nicene Creed, still said in churches today. The Second Council of Nicaea in 787 restored the use of icons after the first wave of iconoclasm.

The Seljuk Turks took it around 1081 and made it their first capital in Anatolia. In 1097 the armies of the First Crusade and the Byzantines took it back in the siege of Nicaea, and the Seljuks moved to Konya.

When crusaders seized Constantinople in 1204, Theodore I Laskaris made Nicaea the capital of a Byzantine state in exile, the Empire of Nicaea. Its rulers retook Constantinople in 1261. The Ottomans captured the city in 1331. Under the name İznik it became famous in the 1500s for its painted tiles and pottery, which cover the walls of the great Ottoman mosques.
sum: An ancient city in northwest Anatolia, on a lake east of the Sea of Marmara, now the small Turkish town of İznik. It is best known for the church councils held there.
